For a fixed candidate set, let E contain item-embedding rows and A=EW. Intervene directly on the scored representation, h′=h+δ, keeping weights, biases and candidates fixed. Then Δs=Aδ. Derivation: the target–competitor margin m_tj=s_t−s_j changes by Δm_tj=(e_t−e_j)ᵀWδ. Biases affect initial margins but cancel from their changes. Measure raw-score changes, centered-score changes and target rank/top-10 membership separately: score dependence need not imply a ranking change. Softmax also ignores common score shifts ([Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.smola.org/slides/tensorflow/chapter_linear-classification/softmax-regression.html)).

Nullspaces distinguish several negative controls. Any δ∈ker(W) leaves projected features and scores unchanged; δ∈ker(A) leaves candidate scores unchanged even if Wδ≠0. With C=I−11ᵀ/n, δ∈ker(CA) gives Aδ=c1: all pairwise margins, rankings and softmax probabilities remain unchanged, although raw scores change when c≠0. Such a nonzero common-shift intervention may not exist. Construct feasible controls with SVD, verify numerical residuals, and report if the required nullspace is trivial. Include a zero intervention and compare perturbations at matched norms.

Positive controls should target observable directions. For scoring, perturb along a nonzero right singular vector of A. For a chosen competitor j, define g=Wᵀ(e_t−e_j); δ=±εg/‖g‖ produces Δm_tj=±ε‖g‖. If g=0, that pair is feature-insensitive. To demonstrate ranking dependence, choose magnitude and sign that cross the actual margin boundary; a small margin change need not reorder items. For top-10 membership, check all competitors after intervention. Compare measured changes with these exact predictions, using deterministic evaluation and the actual scoring path; these tests establish local computational dependence, not semantic causality or recommendation quality.
